Tennis.seoTitle: Club tennis stories: socials, ladders and committees
Tennis.intro: Stories about club tennis from the people who play it, coach it and run it. Social tennis nights, mixers, ladders and box leagues, the championships draw, the committee, and the roller nobody can find. If you play at a tennis club, you'll recognise most of it.

Padel.seoTitle: Padel at tennis clubs: stories from club players
Padel.intro: Padel at a tennis club, from the chair who voted against the courts to the bar argument about whose court is biggest. Padel brings new people into clubs and it's easy to start. The tennis players have opinions about that, and they're in the comments.

Pickleball.seoTitle: Pickleball at tennis clubs: lines, paddles and beginners
Pickleball.intro: Pickleball arriving at tennis clubs: lines painted across tennis courts, beginners' taster sessions with not enough paddles, and coaches who can't decide if they love it or hate it. Mostly they love it. Some of them won't admit it.

Squash.seoTitle: Squash club stories: sessions, software and committees
Squash.intro: Squash club life from the section secretary's side and the court. Running Sunday morning sessions, mixed ability socials, and nineteen meetings about club software that handles payments but still can't tell anyone who wants a game.

Mixers.seoTitle: How to run a social tennis mixer: stories and tips
Mixers.intro: Social tennis mixers, padel socials and pickleball drop-ins, and what actually makes them work. Spread the strong players across the courts, rotate partners, have the draw ready before anyone arrives, and try not to put the county player with the beginner three rounds running.

Organising.seoTitle: Organising social tennis and club sessions
Organising.intro: What it's really like to organise social tennis, squash sessions, ladders and box leagues at a club. Counting heads, chasing replies on WhatsApp, the 6:58pm cancellation, and the organiser who never gets a game at their own tennis night.

Ladders.seoTitle: Tennis ladders: how to run one at your club
Ladders.intro: Running a tennis ladder at a club: the challenge rules you need to agree before you start, what happens when nobody challenges anyone, and why the spreadsheet version nearly always falls over. There's also a bit on ladder vs box league, if you're choosing.

Box leagues.seoTitle: Tennis box leagues: running one at your club
Box leagues.intro: Tennis box leagues at club level: boxes of four or five players, a few weeks to play everyone, promotion and relegation at the end. In practice, nobody plays until the last four days. Stories from the people who run them.

Coaching.seoTitle: Tennis and pickleball coaching stories from club coaches
Coaching.intro: Club coaches on tennis and pickleball coaching: junior sessions, beginners' tasters, parents on the fence, expensive new rackets, and pickleball lines on the court they used to have to themselves.

Beginners.seoTitle: Starting tennis, padel or pickleball as a beginner
Beginners.intro: Starting a racket sport as a beginner, from both sides of the net. A beginner at a mixed ability social who said sorry 46 times, and a coach whose beginners' pickleball taster drew 31 people for eight paddles.

Juniors.seoTitle: Junior tennis: coaches, parents and Saturday sessions
Juniors.intro: Junior tennis from the coach's side: Saturday morning sessions, and the parent who coaches from behind the fence when they could be on the court.

Levels.seoTitle: Mixed ability social tennis and playing levels
Levels.intro: Mixed ability at social tennis, padel and squash: what happens when beginners and strong players end up on the same court, and why playing levels make socials better for everybody.

Finding a game.seoTitle: How to find a tennis partner at your club
Finding a game.intro: Finding someone to play tennis with at your own club is harder than it should be. Stories about Saturday games, partner-finding apps that never worked, and what finally did.

Club life.seoTitle: Tennis club life: committees, courts and the clubhouse
Club life.intro: Everything that happens at a racket club off the court: the committee, the bar, club software, the AGM item about court allocation, padel courts going in, and equipment that goes missing.

Committee.seoTitle: Tennis club committee stories from the chair
Committee.intro: Tennis club committees from the chair's seat. Voting on padel courts, doing the championships draw by hand, working groups about the court roller, and minutes that go nowhere.

Rants.seoTitle: Rants from club tennis, squash and pickleball
Rants.intro: Club players, coaches and secretaries getting things off their chest: box leagues nobody plays, club software meetings, pickleball lines, and £300 rackets that don't fix a backhand.
